Intrinio sits at the higher end, offering rich data and analytics layers, albeit at a premium. Plans are mostly tailored to the requirements with custom pricing, and pricing is volume-based.

**Note:** Real-time pricing is rarely “one number” across providers because the cost usually moves with two things: what you're allowed to stream (coverage and licensing) and how much you're allowed to pull (rate limits, concurrency, and throughput). Many vendors price delayed access as the entry point, then gate live streaming behind a higher plan. Thus, if you're choosing a provider based on cost, don't just look at the base price. Pay attention to how pricing changes as usage grows, and how much of the real-time stack is included upfront.

Choosing a market data API usually looks simple at first.

In practice, that is rarely enough.

Teams usually run into problems later. A provider may look strong on paper, but fall short where it actually matters for the product: coverage may be incomplete, licensing terms may limit what can be shown or redistributed, integration may take more work than expected, or pricing may stop making sense once usage grows.

That is the purpose of this article. This is not a “best API” list. It is a practical scorecard for evaluating six providers: EODHD, Polygon, Intrinio, Twelve Data, Alpha Vantage, and Finnhub.

One thing to be clear about from the start. This article does not rank vendors on speed or uptime through a full benchmark harness. We are not running that comparison here.
